pr_body:
Introduce a new class `QueryTranslatorSpecTests` which uses a text file,
to read and assert translation of planned and optimised queries similar to
the approach already used in EQL.

Furthermore:
 - move the reading/parsing of that file to the common `ql`
module, to avoid repeating code between EQL & SQL.
 - rename test names to remove `_` and words like `Translate`,
or `Painless` which are superfluous.
 - rename EQL tests from `QueryFolderXXXTests` to
 `QueryTranslatorXXXTests`

Closes: #65417
pr_comments: Btw, I think we should include this in 7.13 as well - it's just testing so it doesn't affect shipped code however it will make backporting (if needed) easier.

issue_context.title: QL: Refactor QueryTranslation tests
issue_context.body:
The query translation tests in QL (`QueryTranslatorTests`) and SQL(some bits of `QueryFolderTests`) are done manually which makes them more complicated than they have to be.
Instead of manually extracting the query string, replacing and then comparing it with a string, the test can do this automatically and assert the strings based on an external file based on the approach taken in EQL (`QueryFolderOkTests`) a file that however has an incorrect name.

The two approaches need to be consolidated:
- [x] Use `QueryTranslatorTests` as a name for testing query translation
- [x] Move QL and SQL tests from a manual approach to a declarative approach
- [x] Keep any programmatic test that doesn't just do string comparison into its own test suite
comments: Hello @soarescaique! Thank you for the interest, but we already assigned this work within the team.

review_comments: Any reason why contains need to be specified? Since it's an either/or option - either there's nothing specified (contains) or something else such as regex - specifying contains is redundant.

I kept it, just because it could help when you have multiple assertions of mixed regex and simple contains and could make sense to have something like:
```
contains <match1>
regex <match2>
regex <match3>
contains <match4>
...
```
Since it doesn't complicate the code (it's only a couple of extra lines), I thought it would be nice to have it as an option. If you insist  though I can remove it and keep only the implicit version.
